title: PATRA: Pattern-Aware Alignment and Balanced Reasoning for Time Series Question Answering
claim: Prior approaches flatten the second modality into text or concatenate embeddings; ours decomposes it into patterns and fuses them with a dedicated module.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, progressive complexity, shared legend strip below, dashed divider
description: A wide figure with three side-by-side panels, each showing a way of feeding time series and text to an LLM. Panel (a), single-modality reasoning, converts both inputs into quoted number and word tokens such as "1.1", "3.5" and "What", then passes them to a robot LLM icon with a fire symbol for fine-tuning. Panel (b), shallow alignment, makes separate blue time-series and tan text embeddings. It concatenates them into one column before the LLM. Panel (c), deep alignment, extracts patterns (a seasonal wave and a trend curve) into aligned green TS tokens. It then combines them with text embeddings in an orange Fusion Module, producing fusion tokens for the LLM. A bottom legend defines the token colors. Pastel colors and dashed boxes carry the eye along the arrows to panel (c).
caption: Comparison of alignment paradigms in Time Series Question Answering. (a) Single-Modality Reasoning treats time series as text sequences, converting continuous numerical points into text tokens. (b) Multimodal Shallow Alignment introduces time series as a separate modality but relies on simple concatenation of embeddings. (c) Multimodal Deep Alignment addresses these limitations by explicitly decomposing time series into distinct patterns and fusing them with text embeddings via a dedicated module, ensuring that semantic reasoning is firmly grounded in physical data behaviors.
abstract: Time series reasoning demands both the perception of complex dynamics and logical depth. However, existing LLM-based approaches exhibit two limitations: they often treat time series merely as text or images, failing to capture the patterns like trends and seasonalities needed to answer specific questions; and when trained on a mix of simple and complex tasks, simpler objectives often dominate the learning process, hindering the development of deep reasoning capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose the Pattern-Aware Alignment and Balanced Reasoning model (PATRA), introducing a pattern-aware mechanism that extracts trend and seasonality patterns from time series to achieve deep alignment. Furthermore, we design a task-aware balanced reward to harmonize learning across tasks of varying difficulty, incentivizing the generation of coherent Chains of Thought. Extensive experiments show that PATRA outperforms strong baselines across diverse Time Series Question Answering (TSQA) tasks, demonstrating superior cross-modal understanding and reasoning capability.
